Campus CNRA:
Santa Clara and 4th Streets presently experience noise levels of Ldn 70-80 within the roadway and Ldn 60-70 noise levels extend approximately 200 feet beyond the right-of-way. The Campus area is outside of the aircraft glide pattern noise zone, and is not projected to experience increased noise levels of 1995. Although E. San Fernando Street is a 3-land one-way collector, the San Jose Noise Element shows no present or projected 1990 noise contours.
Gardner CNRA:
The Gardner neighborhood currently experiences high noise readings along Willow Street and a segment of Bird Avenue; and from the Southern Pacific railroad line and Route 280 freeway. Willow Street noise levels of Ldn 70-80 are limited to the immediate roadway with a very small area affected by Ldn 60-70 levels. Bird Avenue from West Virginia Street to the freeway bridge also has a Ldn 70-80 level extending to the roadway edge, with Ldn 60-70 contours less than 100 feet further. The S.P.R.R. line crosses the mid-section of Gardner from east to west and causes Ldn 60-70 levels in a broad area approximately 300 feet each side of the alignment. Noise from the Route 280 freeway is generally restricted due to the depressded alignment, but does affect the westerly edge of the Gardner area, with Ldn 60-70 contours approximately 250 feet from the freeway perimeter. The other dominant noise factor in Gardner is commercial aircraft traffic to and from San Jose Municipal Airport. The westerly edge of the airport glide path is over the easterly edge of Gardner, producing Ldn 60-70 noise levels in the northeasterly section of Gardner in a band 200 to 500 feet wide, as measured from the edge of the future Route 87 alignment.
Future noise levels in Gardner are not projected to improve; rather the conditions will slightly worsen. With the construction of the Guadalupe Freeway (Route 87) Ldn 60-70 noise readings will occur westerly of the freeway approximately from Hull Avenue south to Willow Street. This contour will be approximately 500 feet westerly of the future freeway. Northerly of Hull the depressed design of the freeway will confine the noise to the freeway alignment itself. Increased noise along Bird Avenue from West Virginia Street southerly to Willow Street is also projected in the Noise Element. Levels of Ldn 70-80 are expected along Bird Avenue, with Ldn 60-70 extending about 100 feet each side of the roadway. These projections, however, were based upon the future widening of Bird Avenue southerly of Coe Avenue which would allow for great traffic volumes. The San Jose General Plan eliminated this planned widening; therefore, future traffic volumes and corresponding noise levels may be smaller than projected.
Mayfair CNRA:
The Mayfair neighborhood is surrounded by major thoroughfares and so is affected by vehicular noise. The major noise factor is the Route 680 freeway which forms the southerly and easterly border of the project area.
